title: Logical Operators
learning_outcomes: Explain what logical operators contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: and and or.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Operators combine values into expressions. Parentheses, precedence, strict comparisons, and deliberate fallback behavior help prevent expressions that compile but communicate the wrong intent. In this lesson, focus on and and or; then compare it with not. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use logical operators when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Operators combine values into expressions. Parentheses, precedence, strict comparisons, and deliberate fallback behavior help prevent expressions that compile but communicate the wrong intent. For logical operators, begin with and and or. Also distinguish not; short-circuit evaluation; operator precedence. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Use the smallest representative example, make expected behavior explicit, and test normal plus boundary inputs.

content_blocks.title: Walk through one example
content_blocks.text: Read the example for logical operators from top to bottom. Start by identifying and and or, write down the relevant variable values or control-flow choice, and predict the expected output before running it. Then change one input or condition, check a boundary case, and explain why the result changed.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
